# Hermes v2026.9.11 live session evidence

Captured on Linux amd64 with the official [v2026.9.11 release](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/v2026.9.11), package version 0.21.2, exact source commit `939e45c91d751fadd94dcd1b873ac3cb44846213`. The annotated tag object is `2160b2d59c87316e82f749d77c1f25969bea1533`. The MIT-licensed project supports Python >=3.11,<3.14. The unavailable global shim was bypassed by a temporary Python 3.11.15 environment; no global installation or configuration was changed.

The source archive was fetched from the official GitHub commit archive, extracted with Python's data filter, and installed with existing uv using `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-default-groups --no-python-downloads`. UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT and UV_CACHE_DIR pointed into the temporary capture directory, and UV_PYTHON selected the existing Python 3.11.15 executable. This installed 63 core packages using the release lockfile. `hermes --version` reported Hermes Agent v0.21.2 (2026.9.11), Python 3.11.15 and OpenAI SDK 2.24.0. This is a test environment, not a supported-host installation change.

## Bounded capture

The temporary HERMES_HOME, workspace, subprocess cwd and PWD were explicit. The local OpenAI-compatible Ollama route used `http://localhost:11434/v1` and the user's installed `gemma4:31b-cloud` model, with an existing provider key copied privately without printing it. HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING=0 prevented anonymous guest bootstrap; HERMES_IGNORE_RULES=1 and --ignore-rules excluded ambient rules. Memory, compression and automatic titles were disabled in the private temporary configuration. Only the file toolset was enabled. A private ephemeral instruction prohibited writing files, executing commands or using other tools. The planted workspace file contained `sample value: 42` followed by a newline.

The first command was `hermes chat --oneshot --quiet --ignore-rules --provider custom --model gemma4:31b-cloud --toolsets file --max-turns 3 --run-budget 40 -q 'Read only sample.txt using read_file and answer with its numeric value. Do not use any other tool.'` The second added `--resume 20260912_165604_8bc81a --no-restore-cwd` and requested the same read again. Each owned process group had a 55-second outer timeout followed by at most five seconds for termination. Both exited normally with code 0. Raw logs were private, mode 0600; neither is a fixture.

- First request: 2026-09-12T16:56:02.479464Z through 16:56:12.576872Z.
- Resumed request: 2026-09-12T16:59:14.910016Z through 16:59:19.438183Z.
- The authoritative messages table confirms exactly two `read_file` tool results. The sample file was unchanged. The final session has eight messages, two tool calls and four API calls. These are provenance facts, not additional adapter activity surfaces.

After each process exited, the read-only SQLite source was frozen with SQLite's backup API, which includes committed WAL data. The database was not copied by discarding its WAL. The original session ID `20260912_165604_8bc81a` and all adapter-selected values were preserved. Both snapshots contain the same single session, with counters growing in place:

| Snapshot | Input | Output | Cache read | Cache write | Reasoning | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1796 | 24 | 3776 | 0 | 0 | 5596 |
| After | 3700 | 44 | 7680 | 0 | 0 | 11424 |
| Delta | 1904 | 20 | 3904 | 0 | 0 | 5828 |

The original full-database SHA-256 values are `19a488dad833077a104499513b4edae443790420e6ae34ed78003aa3f8f864be` (before) and `261db11bf41950abf4ca097015570060778f02630e430e3b0f8bdae65fe7442c` (after).

## Sanitization and replay

The SQL fixtures contain the exact captured sessions CREATE TABLE and every value from its captured row. Six content-bearing text columns are replaced with stable planted labels: model_config, system_prompt_hash, cwd, last_activity_description, last_activity_provenance and profile_name. Other tables, including message bodies and system prompts, are excluded because the adapter does not read them. No source ID, model, provider, timestamp, counter, schema name, default, numeric type or NULL state was replaced. Referenced tables are intentionally outside this adapter's fixture surface; SQLite's default disabled foreign-key enforcement permits replay of this session projection.

Both fixtures were loaded into fresh SQLite databases and the ten adapter-selected columns compared directly against the original backups: exact equality, including floating-point timestamps, held for both. SHA-256 over compact Python JSON of the selected tuples in id order is `f0c9d418b4449341679dae2fbeafa2ea81b6d88baf43840e699f9ddb0efbbd82` before and `bfe5702eecff2a32d5f4d08a08bd9e47dc463af41aaa858a7eb0a5ee73c687b1` after. This verifies original-ID and value parity, independently of the sanitized SQL byte hashes checked by the Go oracle:

- live-2026.9.11-before.sql: `2b66e9499bcadeb8ea3b70c80bb949699292252c494bc8030caf297fda15478c`.
- live-2026.9.11-after.sql: `6ad6bebcd17de4f3ae24014db1445bdea723a65bf82d813e4e6f08d9eef2e079`.

`TestLive20260911SnapshotReplayAndDelta` loads both captures, checks original identity, actual timestamps, dimensions and totals, drives the real collector/store through unchanged reads and a growing cumulative snapshot, and proves one 5828-token delta with zero duplicate insertion. It verifies no activity/turn contexts or invented vendor price, and preserves source bytes without new sidecars. Its final reasoning=7 mutation is explicitly constructed, not claimed as nonzero live reasoning.

## Exact writer contract

At the pinned commit, [agent/usage_pricing.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/939e45c91d751fadd94dcd1b873ac3cb44846213/agent/usage_pricing.py#L57-L72) defines canonical prompt tokens as input + cache read + cache write, and total tokens as that sum + output. Lines 481-524 map completion/output counters and reasoning from output/completion detail fields; lines 513-518 subtract cached input from OpenAI prompt totals. This establishes reasoning as an output subset, not a new additive bucket. The adapter's constructed reasoning edge preserves output=44 and total=11424 while emitting reasoning=7.

[agent/turn_usage.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/939e45c91d751fadd94dcd1b873ac3cb44846213/agent/turn_usage.py#L169-L173) adds each canonical bucket into session totals. [hermes_state_usage.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/939e45c91d751fadd94dcd1b873ac3cb44846213/hermes_state_usage.py#L20-L50) generates cumulative delta SQL; lines 275-289 explain that CLI calls increment while gateway absolute assignments supply cumulative totals. The two live captures independently witness growth of the same row. [hermes_state_sessions.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/939e45c91d751fadd94dcd1b873ac3cb44846213/hermes_state_sessions.py#L318-L357) supplies time.time() for REAL started_at; lines 432-438 do so for ended_at.

Required schema anchors are the sessions table and all ten selected columns: id, model, billing_provider, started_at, ended_at, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens and reasoning_tokens. Missing or renamed schema anchors produce ErrSourceFormat without a checkpoint. Selected rows need nonempty id and convertible counters; malformed selected rows retain any valid snapshots but hold the checkpoint. NULL/default-zero counters, optional provider/ended_at and the established NULL/blank-model exclusion remain accepted. Legacy textual timestamps and their fallback order remain supported. `TestLive20260911RequiredSchemaHoldsCheckpoint` and `TestLive20260911OptionalNullCounters` exercise these distinctions.

Hermes computed-cost capability and no-activity declaration remain unchanged. This model has unknown pricing: captured estimated_cost_usd=0, actual_cost_usd=NULL, cost_status=unknown, cost_source=none. Positive vendor cost and nonzero live reasoning are not claimed; reasoning is established by exact writer source plus the constructed edge. The adapter retains its established single session model/project attribution; this capture does not extend support to per-model tables or activity tables.
